name: Agricultural Entrepreneurship

objectives.text: Describe the qualities of a person who starts and runs an agricultural business, such as initiative, persistence, and willingness to take risks
Identify goods and services that local agricultural businesses provide to meet customer needs and wants
Propose an idea for a small agricultural enterprise, such as selling eggs, garden produce, or plants, that meets a need in the local community
Explain the steps involved in starting a small agricultural enterprise, from choosing a product to selling it to customers
Calculate the profit or loss of a simple agricultural enterprise by subtracting expenses from income
Explain how agricultural entrepreneurs obtain the start-up resources they need, including capital, land, equipment, and labor
Explain how an entrepreneur's management decisions affect the land, animals, employees, and community the business depends on
Explain the risks and rewards of agricultural entrepreneurship, including production, market price, and financial risks
Describe how an entrepreneurship SAE differs from a placement SAE in ownership, risk, and decision-making
Analyze the characteristics of successful entrepreneurs in AFNR businesses using interviews or case studies of local producers and agribusiness owners
Write a mission statement and measurable business goals for an agricultural enterprise
Maintain accurate financial and inventory records for an entrepreneurship SAE using a record book system such as AET
Analyze an entrepreneurship SAE as a business model, including its costs, income, return on investment, and management decisions
Compare sole proprietorships, partnerships, limited liability companies, corporations, and cooperatives as ownership structures for a new agricultural business
Conduct a SWOT analysis of a proposed agricultural enterprise to identify its opportunities and risks
Calculate the break-even price and break-even volume for an agricultural product
Evaluate an agricultural business opportunity for its feasibility and potential profitability
Assess alternative production systems for an enterprise's product to select the most profitable and sustainable approach
Develop risk management strategies for an agricultural enterprise, such as insurance, diversification, and forward contracting
Compare sources of start-up financing for young agricultural entrepreneurs, including FSA youth loans, commercial loans, grants, and personal savings
Develop the marketing section of an agricultural business plan, identifying the target market, pricing strategy, and promotion methods
Develop a complete business plan for an original agricultural enterprise, including operations, marketing, financial projections, and management
Evaluate an agricultural business plan for its commercial viability and long-term sustainability
Present and defend an agricultural business concept to a panel of lenders, investors, or judges
Prepare an FFA Agricultural Proficiency or Star in Agribusiness application that documents the growth and financial performance of an entrepreneurship SAE

changes: Kept and reworded all six original objectives, sharpening the risks objective to name production, market, and financial risk and the SAE analysis to include return on investment. Moved the business plan record-keeping clause into its own grade 9 objective on AET records. Added objectives on local goods and services, enterprise idea generation, simple profit calculation, start-up resources, stewardship in management decisions, entrepreneurship versus placement SAE, entrepreneur characteristics analysis, mission statements and goals, ownership structures, SWOT analysis, break-even, production system choice, risk management, start-up financing, the marketing section of a plan, plan evaluation, pitching a concept, and FFA proficiency or Star in Agribusiness applications. Left cooperative operations, workplace skills, and career exploration to sibling sub-topics. Attached AFNR standards only to grade 9 to 12 objectives that directly teach them.
